newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt population 61.45 mln in 1996 - census.
newsitem.headline: Egypt population 61.45 mln in 1996 - census.

text.p: Egypt said on Monday its population growth rate had fallen to 2.1 percent in 1996 from 2.8 percent a decade earlier.

An official census, conducted every 10 years, showed Egypt's inhabitants in 1996 totalled 61.45 million people, making it the the 17th most populous country in the world according to United Nations statistics.
In the 1986 census, the population was 50.504 million. Gender divisions remained steady, with males dominating the population at 51.2 percent against 48.8 percent females.

Only 3.5 percent of Egyptians live outside Egypt. The figures showed that in the 10 years between the two censuses, inhabitants of rural areas mushroomed at a rate of 2.26 percent while urban areas had lower growth rates at 1.85 percent.
The census also showed that children under the age of six were the second largest population group at 15.1 percent.
Cairo, one of Africa's largest cities, the population grew between 1986 and 1996 by 11.9 percent to 6.79 million.
But the figures referred only to the city of Cairo, ignoring the inhabitants of Greater Cairo, which includes several suburbs and which swells the city's population to about 17 million.
The census was conducted by the government's Central Agency for Population, Mobilisation and Statistics (CAPMAS) for six months from June 1, 1996.
